metadata.title: CSS Injection via bypassSecurityTrustStyle on Server-Supplied field.style

transformations: field.style passed to DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustStyle() with no validation

privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: CSS injection into user browser — data exfiltration via CSS url() trick

impact.description: CSS injection via bypassSecurityTrustStyle allows server to inject arbitrary CSS including url() exfiltration via CSS-based data theft. Scope changed to Unchanged as injection stays in user context. Both InputFieldComponent and FieldComponent affected.

remediation.fix_approach: Removed bypassSecurityTrustStyle() from both InputFieldComponent.getCss() and FieldComponent.getCss(). Replaced with a CSS property allowlist parser returning a plain {[key:string]:string} object. Angular [style] binding applies this safely without any security bypass. Added value-level url()/expression()/javascript: guard as defense-in-depth.

attack_chains: VULN-001 → VULN-008: CSS injection enables XSS token exfil

history.note: bypassSecurityTrustStyle used on server-supplied field.style in InputFieldComponent.getCss() and FieldComponent.getCss() — CSS injection via url() exfiltration possible

CONFIRMED: CSS injection via bypassSecurityTrustStyle in both InputFieldComponent and FieldComponent. CVSS refined to 5.9 MEDIUM (Scope Unchanged). Attack chain: VULN-001 → VULN-008 for session token exfil.

FIXED: bypassSecurityTrustStyle() removed from both components. getCss() now returns a plain CSS property object filtered through an 18-property allowlist with additional url()/expression()/javascript: value guard. DomSanitizer import and injection removed entirely. Zero bypassSecurityTrust* calls remain in codebase. Pending rescan and manual testing verification.
